record.paper_title: Research Problems on Relations Between Nijenhuis Geometry and Integrable Systems
record.original_question: Given a Nijenhuis operator L, describe all of its local conservation laws.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.1. Given a Nijenhuis operator L, describe all of its (local) conservation laws

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold and let $L: TM \to TM$ be a Nijenhuis operator on $M$, that is, a (1,1)-tensor field whose Nijenhuis torsion
$$\mathcal{N}_L(X,Y) := L^2[X,Y] - L[LX,Y] - L[X,LY] + [LX,LY]$$
vanishes identically for all vector fields $X,Y$ on $M$.

A local conservation law of $L$ is a smooth function $f$ defined on an open set $U \subseteq M$ such that the differential $df$ satisfies
$$L^*(df) = d g$$
for some smooth function $g$ on $U$, where $L^*$ denotes the dual endomorphism of $T^*M$. Equivalently, $df$ is a closed 1-form such that $L^* df$ is also closed.

Problem: Given an arbitrary Nijenhuis operator $L$, give a complete description of the space of all local conservation laws of $L$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of describing all local conservation laws of an arbitrary Nijenhuis operator is in general open. Substantial partial results exist: for gl-regular Nijenhuis operators at algebraically generic points, a complete description of symmetries and conservation laws has been obtained via first/second companion coordinates, and a splitting theorem has been established. The general (non-gl-regular, singular) case remains an open research problem.

status_evidence.title: Nijenhuis geometry IV: conservation laws, symmetries and integration of certain non-diagonalisable systems of hydrodynamic type in quadratures
status_evidence.snippet: Provides explicit description of all symmetries and conservation laws for gl-regular Nijenhuis operators at algebraically generic points.
status_evidence.claim: Partial solution exists in the gl-regular case.

status_evidence.title: Nijenhuis Geometry: Open Problems (Lecture 21)
status_evidence.snippet: Open problems lecture in the Nijenhuis geometry program by Bolsinov and Konyaev.
status_evidence.claim: Describing conservation laws of Nijenhuis operators is listed as an active research problem.
